Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal. And though I have the gift of prophecy, and understand all mysteries, and all knowledge; and though I have all faith, so that I could remove mountains, and have not charity, I am nothing. And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing. Charity suffereth long, and is kind; charity envieth not; charity vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up, Doth not behave itself unseemly, seeketh not her own, is not easily provoked, thinketh no evil; Rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth; Beareth all things, believeth all things, hopeth all things, endureth all things. Charity never faileth: but whether there be prophecies, they shall fail; whether there be tongues, they shall cease; whether there be knowledge, it shall vanish away. For we know in part, and we prophesy in part. But when that which is perfect is come, then that which is in part shall be done away. When I was a child, I spake as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child: but when I became a man, I put away childish things. For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known. And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity –1 Corinthians 13:1-13.

Several years ago, my nephew was quite busy for a number of months building a house for himself and his soon-to-be bride. I’d like to compare that to the building of a marriage. As you know when you build a house you need to have a blueprint to follow. So it is when we build a marriage; we need to follow the blueprint of God’s Word. We all know that the first step in building a house is to lay a good foundation. So it is with marriage. For all of you who are married, I trust you have been, and will continue building your marriage on the foundation of Jesus Christ. There are many elements to a strong house that we could compare to a strong marriage but today I want to think about what it is that gives power to your house or power to a marriage—that thing is called love.

I want to look at nine elements of love:

1. Patience

Love suffereth long. Love is ready to do the work of love whenever the need arises. It is never in a hurry, instead it wears the ornaments of a meek and a quiet spirit. It will wait for the perfect opportunity and will, in the best way, quietly instruct, or exemplify, the purposes of God before your family, before your church, and before your spouse. Sometimes you are going to have to do it for a long time… alone. It will not falter in times of difficulty. A patient person is a predictable person. Love is patiently persistent; it does not abide in the temporal but in the realm of the eternal. Love understands this; therefore, love waits. It can take a long time for a human to surrender to the Lordship of Christ. That time will be shortened in perspective when a man of faith exemplifies a life of obedience and sacrifice in patience. Patience is the normal attitude of love.

2. Kindness

Kindness is love in action! The greatest thing a man can do for his Heavenly Father is to be kind to his Father’s other children. This is not hard to do, and the world needs it. To every married man reading this article, I ask that you consider this—if you would lead your wife on the journey of love, you cannot do it successfully if you try to do it without the element of kindness. Kindness makes living out the purposes of God attractive to those looking on! It will go a long way in helping your wife to draw near to God because she sees the profound effects of that nearness on her husband’s life. How kind has God been to you in bringing salvation to you? Buying woodworking tools and automotive equipment for your wife’s birthday will not promote a healthy marriage. As her husband, you must seek to enrich her life, not yours. Kindness is a normal attitude of love.

3. Generosity

Love envieth not! The opposite of envy is “generosity”. The opposite of generosity is greed, bitterness, covetousness, and spite. Husbands, you might be able to identify with me when I say that in every labor there will be other people who are engaging in the same toil as you are and probably doing it better. What complicates things is when that better person is your wife. Here the temptation is to develop a mood of ill-will and covetousness. How often do we do little things to throw a wrench in the works out of a spirit of envy, for no other reason than to destroy her good works so that she doesn’t outshine us?

There is only one character trait that a Christian should envy. That is to possess a rich and generous soul which envieth not. How many people have become discouraged from wholly following Christ because I withheld from them the needed tools for success out of jealous envy? Our family owns a cabinet shop. Carrying cabinets puts people in a vulnerable position. If envy rules, subtle things like carrying a cabinet awkwardly can hinder the work. Pinching someone’s fingers in a tight doorway is a perfect way to reduce my foe down to his size and the work successfully is hindered, and I can still maintain my innocence. How many marriages and churches operate with these kinds of sins, week after week? Husbands don’t be angry with your wife when she ends up being smarter than you are in a certain matter. In this she has not committed an error or a fault. My friends, what resources has God withheld from you that keeps you from being victorious in that great plan of redemption? Has He not been generous? Generosity is a normal attitude of love.

4. Humility

Love vaunteth not itself, is not puffed up. After you have been patient, kind, and generous and love has done its beautiful work in the world, go back into the shadows and say nothing about it. Human nature has a tendency to exalt itself which only succeeds in stopping love in its tracks because self-exultation is so contrary to love’s divine nature. The scripture commands us to, Let another man praise thee, and not thine own mouth; a stranger, and not thine own lips. –Proverbs 27:2. How many times have I spoiled an opportunity to further the work of God in another person’s life because I got in between God’s love and their heart, and they were offended?

Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall –Proverbs 16:18.

A man’s pride shall bring him low: but honour shall uphold the humble in spirit –Proverbs 29:23.

Pride will destroy the work of God and it will destroy any effort to love my brother or sister. Humility is a normal attitude of love, and it assists love greatly in its eternal purposes.

5. Courtesy

Love doth not behave itself unseemly. This is love in relation to etiquette. The NIV says it better. “Love is not rude! Courtesy is love in the little things.” I want all of us to think of a particular word. It is the word “gentleman.” The word ‘gentleman’ is a compound word, and it literally means “gentle man”. By definition, it simply defines a man who does things gently. A man who does not possess this quality can do nothing less than to be ungentle, unsympathetic, and rude. He cannot help it.

Married brothers... You will not guide your spouse into experiencing the love of God if your heart is devoid of courtesy for your wife. Courtesy is the grace that shows a special tenderness and respect for a fellow human being. I have knowledge of a sad marriage which started badly. The groom’s brash boast was that his in-laws may as well get to know him sooner than later. He started out very early on, expressing himself rudely at the supper table. It is no wonder that after the honeymoon was over his wife found him to be a man she didn’t want to live with and for good reason. The marriage didn’t continue “happily ever after” because there was a complete lack of courtesy. Courtesy is a normal attitude of love.

6. Unselfishness

Love seeketh not her own. Or we could say it this way—love will not attempt to snatch that which belongs to me, even by right. There will come a day when a man or a woman, in the name of biblical love, must exercise a higher calling of giving up his own personal rights in order to advance the kingdom of God. Love strikes us deeply in the area of unselfishness. It is a very difficult thing after we have purchased our rights, won them, dreamed about them, desired them, and sacrificed for them, to need to give them up. And yet love will relinquish it all so that the purposes of God might be pre-eminent. Only for the great and noble purposes of divine love can we justify the waste of having given up that which we naturally perceive belongs to us by right. No sacrifice is too hard for love to make. True love will enjoy what is given but its very nature cannot take that which is not voluntarily offered. Love is the path to life and freedom. There is no happiness in getting but only in giving. Many marriages exist with the attitude that happiness comes in having or in getting, but that is not God’s way. There would be few divorces if a husband worked as hard to keep his wife as he did to get her in the first place. Unselfishness is a normal attitude of love.

7. Good Temper

Love is not easily provoked. There are many decent, hardworking moral people in this world who are fatally flawed by being touchy and ill tempered—they have a short fuse. Few things unchristianize a good man than an evil temper. This sinful character flaw devastates the home, saps the vitality of men and women he rubs shoulders with, and it corrupts the beauty and innocence of his children. This misery-producing power stands alone. It is made up of jealousy, anger, pride, cruelty, self-righteousness, touchiness, doggedness, sullenness... These all make up the character of a loveless soul. Someone once said; There is no place in heaven for a man like this; for to enter into heaven a man must take himself along. My friends, the home is like hell on earth when an individual of this caliber is at the helm. A grouch is a man who sizes himself up and is sore about it.

Temper is significant. A man is no bigger than the thing that makes him angry. It is not so much about what a temper is, but what it reveals about what is inside a person. It reveals a lack of generosity, courtesy, and unselfishness. A lack of patience, and a lack of kindness, are instantaneously symbolized in one flash of temper. It is not enough to deal with the surface symptom of temper. We must go to the source and allow the Lord Jesus Christ to change us from the deepest depth of our nature, and the anger in our souls will die by itself. How many children want nothing to do with Christianity because of an evil temper in the heart of a father or a mother?! We really have no time to lose. It is with patient persistence that a wife, a husband, or a pastor must love this moral despot. For he too must be conquered by the redemptive love of Jesus Christ. This is the purpose of love. To be tempered by the power of God is a normal attitude of love.

8. Quality or ability to “think no evil”

The people who inspire me are the people who believe in me and encourage me. It is also true that in an atmosphere of suspicion and mistrust, people shrivel up and die. In the absence of trust and goodwill, love cannot exist, let alone thrive. Nothing makes a marriage rust like distrust. It is a delightful and a wonderful thing to find people in this loveless world who assume the best about another person until it is proven otherwise. How often I have found in life that I was wrong about the motives of another person! The quickest way to destroy love in marriage is to assume something negative about the motives of your spouse when only the Lord knows the heart. Divine love wants the object of its focus to succeed and not to fall on its face and fail.

Is it possible that if we would succeed in elevating others to new heights, we would find that our own success is enhanced by our vision or belief of what that person could become? Is it possible that good, old-fashioned respect for the object of our love is the first step to restoring the self-respect a man has lost? If we treat our spouses dishonorably and with disrespect, there is a good chance they will become or remain the person we detest. Someone once said “Sisters, a happy wife sometimes has the best husband, but more often she makes the best out of the husband she has.” You see, man was made in the image of God and the greatest thing you can do for a person is to use the power of love to aid in the restoration of what has been lost. The Son of man came to seek and to save that which was lost. Thinking no evil is a normal attitude of love.

9. Sincerity

Brothers and sisters, we get it so backwards. A man who knows the love of Christ chooses the high road to make wrongs right. It is his highest delight to see the purposes of God practically worked out in another person’s life, not the other way around. How often we delight to see our enemy fall. Destructive criticism and an over-focus on the faults or sins of others weakens their ability to overcome. Overplaying and capitalizing on the faults of others hinders our marriages and churches from being filled with overcoming people. Couples, whatever it is that you believe about your spouse is probably what he or she will become.

Those who truly love others are filled with delight and rejoicing when they examine a situation and find out things were better than they had feared.

Love and trust go hand in hand. Because my soul is secure in the hands of an unchanging God, I can safely reach out in sincerity to those who have entered into the realm of influence. Rejoicing in righteousness and thinking NO EVIL is a normal and final attitude of love.

The Greatness of Love (the Greatest Thing in the World)

a.) It bears all things

Brothers, can you bear all things for the sake of redemptive love and its eternal purposes? When you are tempted to quit loving, remember what Jesus bore for you. The ability to bear all things is a normal attitude of love. Can you take an insult without returning one? Even the devil has the wisdom to patiently endure if it gives him a greater future advantage.

b.) It hopeth all things

And hope maketh not ashamed; because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us –Romans 5:5.

Sisters, if your husband falls short of the glory you married him with, can you wait patiently for the Lord to work in his life? When your husband surprises you by being a different person than you thought you married, practice seeing him for what he could be instead of what he isn’t and then encourage him in hope rather than discourage him with hopelessness.

c.) It endureth all things.

Therefore I endure all things for the elect’s sakes, that they may also obtain the salvation which is in Christ Jesus with eternal glory –2 Timothy 2:10.

O give thanks unto the LORD; for he is good; for his mercy endureth for ever –1 Chronicles 16:34.

Brothers and sisters, how long is your endurance? When you get tired of enduring, remember how long God endures with you. Most matrimonial troubles come when two people choose to not endure because they are in love with themselves instead of their spouse.

d.) It never faileth because God is the source of it.

Prophecies fail.

Tongues fail.

Knowledge vanishes away.

True biblical love never gives up. It never fails; therefore, it can never be defeated.

Love cannot be achieved through the eloquence of words. It cannot be seized by willpower. It cannot be learned through education, and it cannot be purchased through human sacrifice. It is not for sale, nor can it be traded like a commodity for it is spiritual in nature. Love can only be received from the Great Eternal Giver, to those worthy to possess such power and glory in their hearts.

The sincerity of my personal quest to pursue and to comprehend from the heart, the love of Christ, will determine the quantity and the quality of love for others. It was Paul’s sincere cry to the Philippians “...that I might know him”.

Husbands and wives, when you first met each other, your love was very immature. You saw it as through a glass darkly or as a poor reflection in the mirror. You spoke about the future of your love like immature children who had no experience with it. You began knowing about it and you prophesied about it. Now that you are married, you know a lot more about LOVE than you did, but there is so much more still to learn. My friends, may the looking glass become clearer for you with maturity and may you understand love in its perfection in the days to come. But the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day –Proverbs 4:18.

Husbands and wives, the best thing you can do for each other is to pursue a daily relationship with the Lord Jesus Christ. Remember that any success in life requires practice. Practice loving each other. Be patient, be kind, be generous, be humble, be unselfish. In all sincerity encourage each other to surrender your hearts to the Lordship of Jesus Christ and your marriage will be above and beyond everything you have ever imagined. A young man once prayed... “Lord, send me a wife that loves you for I know that if she loves you, she will also love me.” He was a wise man.

Great love comes at a great cost. It cost the Lord Jesus Christ His life. Only after you have given your hearts to the Lord in complete trust, will you be able to give your hearts to each other. You have already gained everything; therefore, you have nothing to lose by giving your all in an earthly relationship. That is the cost of love, and it is worth it. Love is life and life is love. It is better not to live than to not love. If love is present in your home, you will find energetic purpose for living and all will be well. Place your hope and faith in the God of Love and you will find... the Greatest Thing in the World.

Beloved, let us love one another: for love is of God; and every one that loveth is born of God, and knoweth God –1 John 4:7.

For whatsoever is born of God overcometh the world: and this is the victory that overcometh the world, even our faith –1 John 5:4.

May God bless every bride and groom.

Die liefde is lankmoedig en vriendelik; die liefde is nie afgunstig nie; die liefde spog nie, is nie opgeblase nie, gedra haar nie onwelvoeglik nie, soek nie haar eie belang nie, word nie maklik uitgelok nie, reken die kwaad nie toe nie; is nie bly oor ongeregtigheid nie, maar is bly saam met die waarheid; bedek alles, glo alles, hoop alles, verdra alles. Die liefde vergaan nooit nie; maar profesieë—dit sal ophou; tale—dit sal ophou; kennis—dit sal verdwyn. Want ons ken gedeeltelik en ons profeteer gedeeltelik. Maar wanneer die volmaakte gekom het, sal wat gedeeltelik is, tot ’n einde kom. Toe ek ’n kind was, het ek soos ’n kind gepraat, soos ’n kind verstaan, soos ’n kind gedink; maar toe ek ’n man geword het, het ek die dinge van ’n kind afgelê. Want nou sien ons deur ’n spieël, dof; maar dan van aangesig tot aangesig. Nou ken ek gedeeltelik; maar dan sal ek ten volle ken, net soos ek ook ten volle geken is. En nou bly geloof, hoop, liefde—hierdie drie; maar die grootste hiervan is die liefde –1 Korintiërs 13:1-13.

’n Paar jaar gelede was my neef ’n hele paar maande lank besig om vir homself en sy aanstaande bruid ’n huis te bou. Ek wil dit graag vergelyk met die bou van ’n huwelik. Soos julle weet, moet ’n mens ’n bouplan volg wanneer jy ’n huis bou. Net so moet ons die bouplan van God se Woord volg wanneer ons ’n huwelik bou. Ons weet almal dat die eerste stap met die bou van ’n huis is om ’n goeie fondament te lê. So is dit ook met die huwelik. Aan almal van julle wat getroud is: ek vertrou dat julle julle huwelik op die fondament van Jesus Christus gebou het en sal aanhou bou. Daar is baie dinge aan ’n sterk huis wat ons met ’n sterk huwelik kan vergelyk, maar vandag wil ek dink aan dit wat krag aan ’n huis of aan ’n huwelik gee—daardie ding word liefde genoem.

Ek wil na nege elemente van liefde kyk:

1. Geduld

Die liefde is lankmoedig. Liefde is gereed om die werk van liefde te doen wanneer die behoefte ook al ontstaan. Dit is nooit haastig nie; dit dra eerder die versierings van ’n sagmoedige en stille gees. Dit sal wag vir die volmaakte geleentheid en sal, op die beste manier, stilweg die oogmerke van God aan jou gesin, jou kerk en jou huweliksmaat verduidelik of voorleef. Soms sal jy dit lank moet doen… alleen. Dit sal nie in moeilike tye wankel nie. ’n Geduldige mens is voorspelbaar. Liefde volhard geduldig; dit vertoef nie in die tydelike nie, maar in die sfeer van die ewige. Liefde verstaan dit; daarom wag liefde. Dit kan ’n lang tyd neem voordat ’n mens hom aan die heerskappy van Christus onderwerp. Vanuit ’n ander perspektief lyk dié tyd korter wanneer ’n man van geloof in geduld ’n lewe van gehoorsaamheid en selfopoffering voorleef. Geduld is die normale gesindheid van liefde.

2. Vriendelikheid

Vriendelikheid is liefde in aksie! Die grootste ding wat ’n man vir sy Hemelse Vader kan doen, is om vriendelik te wees teenoor sy Vader se ander kinders. Dit is nie moeilik nie, en die wêreld het dit nodig. Aan elke getroude man wat hierdie artikel lees, vra ek dat jy hieroor sal nadink—as jy jou vrou op die liefdesreis wil lei, kan jy dit nie suksesvol doen as jy die element van vriendelikheid probeer nalaat nie. Vriendelikheid maak dit aantreklik vir dié wat toekyk om God se oogmerke uit te leef! Dit sal baie help om jou vrou nader aan God te laat kom, omdat sy die diepgaande uitwerking van daardie nabyheid op haar man se lewe sien. Hoe vriendelik was God teenoor jou toe Hy jou verlossing gebring het? Om vir jou vrou se verjaarsdag houtwerk- en motorwerktuigtoerusting te koop, sal nie ’n gesonde huwelik bevorder nie. As haar man moet jy haar lewe probeer verryk, nie joune nie. Vriendelikheid is ’n normale gesindheid van liefde.

3. Vrygewigheid

Die liefde is nie afgunstig nie! Die teenoorgestelde van afguns is “vrygewigheid”. Die teenoorgestelde van vrygewigheid is gierigheid, bitterheid, hebsug en nyd. Mans, julle sal my dalk verstaan wanneer ek sê dat daar in elke soort werk ander mense is wat dieselfde moeite as jy doen en dit waarskynlik beter doen. Dinge raak ingewikkeld wanneer daardie beter persoon jou vrou is. Dan is daar die versoeking om ’n gesindheid van kwaadwilligheid en hebsug te ontwikkel. Hoe dikwels doen ons klein dingetjies om ’n stokkie in die wiel te steek uit afguns—om geen ander rede as om haar goeie werk te bederf sodat sy ons nie oortref nie?

Daar is net een karaktereienskap waarna ’n Christen afgunstig behoort te wees: om ’n ryk en vrygewige siel te hê wat nie afgunstig is nie. Hoeveel mense het moed opgegee om Christus heelhartig te volg omdat ek uit jaloerse afguns die nodige hulpmiddels vir hulle sukses van hulle weerhou het? Ons gesin besit ’n kabinetmakery. Wanneer mense kaste dra, plaas dit hulle in ’n kwesbare posisie. As afguns die oorhand kry, kan subtiele dinge soos om ’n kas ongemaklik te dra, die werk belemmer. Om iemand se vingers in ’n nou deurkosyn vas te knyp, is ’n volmaakte manier om my teenstander tot sy grootte af te bring; die werk word belemmer, en ek kan steeds onskuldig voorkom. Hoeveel huwelike en kerke funksioneer week ná week met hierdie soort sondes? Mans, moenie kwaad wees vir julle vrou wanneer sy uiteindelik slimmer as julle blyk te wees in ’n bepaalde saak nie. Hierin het sy geen fout of oortreding begaan nie. My vriende, watter hulpbronne het God van julle weerhou wat julle daarvan weerhou om oorwinnaars te wees in daardie groot verlossingsplan? Was Hy dan nie vrygewig nie? Vrygewigheid is ’n normale gesindheid van liefde.

4. Nederigheid

Die liefde spog nie, is nie opgeblase nie. Nadat jy geduldig, vriendelik en vrygewig was en liefde sy mooi werk in die wêreld gedoen het, gaan terug in die skaduwees en sê niks daaroor nie. Die menslike natuur is geneig om homself te verhef, wat net daarin slaag om liefde tot stilstand te bring, want selfverheffing is so strydig met die goddelike natuur van liefde. Die Skrif beveel ons: Laat ’n ander jou prys, en nie jou eie mond nie; ’n vreemdeling, en nie jou eie lippe nie. –Spreuke 27:2. Hoeveel keer het ek ’n geleentheid bederf om God se werk in iemand anders se lewe te bevorder, omdat ek tussen God se liefde en daardie persoon se hart kom staan het, en hy aanstoot geneem het?

’n Man se hoogmoed sal hom verneder, maar eer sal die nederige van gees ondersteun –Spreuke 29:23.

Hoogmoed sal God se werk vernietig en elke poging om my broer of suster lief te hê, vernietig. Nederigheid is ’n normale gesindheid van liefde, en dit help liefde baie om sy ewige oogmerke te bereik.

5. Hoflikheid

Die liefde gedra haar nie onwelvoeglik nie. Dit is liefde in verband met goeie maniere. Die NIV stel dit beter. “Liefde is nie onbeskof nie! Hoflikheid is liefde in die klein dingetjies.” Ek wil hê ons almal moet aan ’n bepaalde woord dink. Dit is die woord “gentleman”. Die woord “gentleman” is ’n samestelling en beteken letterlik “sagte man”. Volgens die definisie is dit eenvoudig ’n man wat dinge sagkens doen. ’n Man wat nie hierdie eienskap het nie, kan nie anders as om hardvogtig, onsimpatiek en onbeskof te wees nie. Hy kan dit nie help nie.

Getroude broers... Julle sal nie julle huweliksmaat lei om God se liefde te ervaar as julle hart nie hoflikheid teenoor julle vrou bevat nie. Hoflikheid is die genade wat besondere teerheid en respek teenoor ’n medemens toon. Ek ken ’n hartseer huwelik wat sleg begin het. Die bruidegom se astrante grootpratery was dat sy skoonfamilie hom maar eerder vroeër as later moes leer ken. Van vroeg af het hy hom onbeskof aan die etenstafel uitgedruk. Dit is geen wonder dat sy vrou hom ná die wittebrood as ’n man beskou het met wie sy nie wou saamleef nie, en met goeie rede. Die huwelik het nie “vir ewig gelukkig” voortgeduur nie, omdat daar ’n algehele gebrek aan hoflikheid was. Hoflikheid is ’n normale gesindheid van liefde.

6. Onselfsugtigheid

Die liefde soek nie haar eie belang nie. Of ons kan dit só stel—liefde sal nie probeer gryp wat aan my behoort nie, selfs nie iets waarop ek ’n reg het nie. Daar sal ’n dag kom wanneer ’n man of ’n vrou, in die naam van Bybelse liefde, ’n hoër roeping sal moet uitleef deur sy of haar eie persoonlike regte prys te gee om God se koninkryk te bevorder. Liefde tref ons diep op die gebied van onselfsugtigheid. Dit is baie moeilik om ons regte prys te gee nadat ons dit opgeëis, verower, daaroor gedroom, daarna verlang en daarvoor opgeoffer het. En tog sal liefde alles prysgee sodat God se oogmerke die voorrang kan hê. Slegs ter wille van die groot en edele oogmerke van goddelike liefde kan ons die verlies regverdig wanneer ons opgee wat ons natuurlik as ons regmatige eiendom beskou. Geen opoffering is vir liefde te swaar nie. Ware liefde sal geniet wat gegee word, maar dit lê nie in sy aard om te neem wat nie vrywillig aangebied word nie. Liefde is die pad na lewe en vryheid. Daar is geen geluk daarin om te kry nie, maar net daarin om te gee. Baie huwelike bestaan met die gesindheid dat geluk daarin lê om te hê of te kry, maar dit is nie God se manier nie. Daar sou min egskeidings wees as ’n man net so hard gewerk het om sy vrou te behou as wat hy aanvanklik gewerk het om haar te kry. Onselfsugtigheid is ’n normale gesindheid van liefde.

7. ’n Goeie humeur

Die liefde word nie maklik uitgelok nie. Daar is baie ordentlike, hardwerkende, sedelike mense in hierdie wêreld wat noodlottig gebrekkig is omdat hulle liggeraak en humeurig is—hulle lont is kort. Min dinge maak ’n goeie man so onchristelik soos ’n slegte humeur. Hierdie sondige karaktergebrek verwoes die huis, tap die lewenskrag van mans en vroue met wie hy omgaan, en verderf die skoonheid en onskuld van sy kinders. Hierdie vermoë om ellende te veroorsaak, staan op sy eie. Dit bestaan uit jaloesie, woede, hoogmoed, wreedheid, eiegeregtigheid, liggeraaktheid, hardnekkigheid, norsheid... Al hierdie dinge vorm die karakter van ’n liefdelose siel. Iemand het eens gesê: Daar is geen plek in die hemel vir ’n man soos hierdie nie; want om die hemel binne te gaan, moet ’n man homself saamneem. My vriende, ’n huis is soos die hel op aarde wanneer iemand van hierdie kaliber aan die stuur is. ’n Norse mens is iemand wat homself takseer en daaroor ontsteld is.

’n Mens se humeur is belangrik. ’n Man is nie groter as die ding wat hom kwaad maak nie. Dit gaan nie soseer oor wat ’n humeur is nie, maar oor wat dit openbaar van wat binne-in ’n mens is. Dit openbaar ’n gebrek aan vrygewigheid, hoflikheid en onselfsugtigheid. ’n Gebrek aan geduld en vriendelikheid word onmiddellik in een woede-uitbarsting weerspieël. Dit is nie genoeg om die oppervlakkige simptoom van ’n slegte humeur te hanteer nie. Ons moet na die bron gaan en die Here Jesus Christus toelaat om ons diepste natuur te verander; dan sal die woede in ons siel vanself sterf. Hoeveel kinders wil niks met die Christendom te doen hê nie weens ’n slegte humeur in die hart van ’n vader of moeder?! Ons het werklik nie tyd om te verloor nie. Dit is met geduldige volharding dat ’n vrou, ’n man of ’n leraar hierdie sedelike despoot moet liefhê. Want ook hy moet deur die verlossende liefde van Jesus Christus oorwin word. Dit is die doel van liefde. Om deur die krag van God getemper te word, is ’n normale gesindheid van liefde.

8. Die eienskap of vermoë om “geen kwaad te bedink nie”

Die mense wat my inspireer, is die mense wat in my glo en my aanmoedig. Dit is ook waar dat mense in ’n atmosfeer van agterdog en wantroue wegkwyn en sterf. Sonder vertroue en welwillendheid kan liefde nie bestaan nie, wat nog te sê floreer. Niks laat ’n huwelik so roes soos wantroue nie. Dit is ’n wonderlike en vreugdevolle ding om in hierdie liefdelose wêreld mense te vind wat die beste van ’n ander persoon aanneem totdat die teendeel bewys is. Hoe dikwels het ek in die lewe agtergekom dat ek verkeerd was oor ’n ander persoon se beweegredes! Die vinnigste manier om liefde in die huwelik te vernietig, is om iets negatiefs oor jou huweliksmaat se beweegredes aan te neem, terwyl net die Here die hart ken. Goddelike liefde wil hê dat die persoon op wie dit gerig is, suksesvol moet wees, nie dat hy plat op sy gesig moet val en misluk nie.

Is dit moontlik dat ons, as ons daarin slaag om ander tot nuwe hoogtes te verhef, sal ontdek dat ons eie sukses bevorder word deur ons visie van of geloof in wat daardie persoon kan word? Is dit moontlik dat goeie, outydse respek vir die persoon wat ons liefhet die eerste stap is om ’n man se verlore selfrespek te herstel? As ons ons huweliksmaats oneerbaar en sonder respek behandel, is die kans goed dat hulle die persoon sal word of bly wat ons verag. Iemand het eens gesê: “Susters, ’n gelukkige vrou het soms die beste man, maar meer dikwels maak sy die beste van die man wat sy het.” Kyk, die mens is na die beeld van God geskape, en die grootste ding wat jy vir iemand kan doen, is om die krag van liefde te gebruik om te help herstel wat verlore gegaan het. Die Seun van die mens het gekom om te soek en te red wat verlore was. Om geen kwaad te bedink nie, is ’n normale gesindheid van liefde.

9. Opregtheid

Broers en susters, ons verstaan dit heeltemal verkeerd. ’n Man wat die liefde van Christus ken, kies die regte pad om onreg reg te stel. Sy grootste vreugde is om te sien hoe God se oogmerke prakties in iemand anders se lewe verwesenlik word, nie andersom nie. Hoe dikwels verheug ons ons wanneer ons vyand val. Vernietigende kritiek en ’n oormatige fokus op ander se foute of sondes verswak hulle vermoë om dit te bowe te kom. Om ander se foute te oordryf en uit te buit, verhinder dat ons huwelike en kerke gevul word met mense wat oorwin. Paartjies, wat julle ook al oor julle huweliksmaat glo, sal waarskynlik bepaal wat hy of sy word.

Dié wat ander waarlik liefhet, is vol vreugde en blydskap wanneer hulle ’n situasie ondersoek en ontdek dat dinge beter was as waarvoor hulle gevrees het.

Liefde en vertroue gaan hand aan hand. Omdat my siel veilig is in die hande van ’n onveranderlike God, kan ek my opreg uitstrek na dié wat binne my invloedsfeer gekom het. Om jou oor geregtigheid te verheug en GEEN KWAAD TE BEDINK NIE, is ’n normale en laaste gesindheid van liefde.

Die grootheid van liefde (die grootste ding in die wêreld)

a.) Dit bedek alles

Broers, kan julle alles verdra ter wille van verlossende liefde en die ewige oogmerke daarvan? Wanneer julle in die versoeking kom om op te hou liefhê, onthou wat Jesus vir julle verdra het. Die vermoë om alles te verdra, is ’n normale gesindheid van liefde. Kan jy ’n belediging verdra sonder om een terug te gee? Selfs die duiwel is wys genoeg om geduldig te volhard as dit hom ’n groter toekomstige voordeel oplewer.

b.) Dit hoop alles

En die hoop beskaam nie, omdat die liefde van God in ons harte uitgestort is deur die Heilige Gees wat aan ons gegee is –Romeine 5:5.

Susters, as julle man nie voldoen aan die heerlikheid waarmee julle met hom getrou het nie, kan julle geduldig wag dat die Here in sy lewe werk? Wanneer julle man julle verras deur anders te wees as die persoon met wie julle gedink het julle trou, oefen dan om hom te sien vir wat hy kan wees eerder as vir wat hy nie is nie, en moedig hom dan met hoop aan eerder as om hom met hopeloosheid te ontmoedig.

c.) Dit verdra alles.

Daarom verdra ek alles ter wille van die uitverkorenes, sodat ook hulle die verlossing wat in Christus Jesus is, met ewige heerlikheid kan verkry –2 Timoteus 2:10.

Dank die HERE, want Hy is goed; want sy goedertierenheid is tot in ewigheid –1 Kronieke 16:34.

Broers en susters, hoe lank hou julle vol? Wanneer julle moeg word daarvan om te volhard, onthou hoe lank God met julle volhard. Die meeste huweliksprobleme ontstaan wanneer twee mense besluit om nie te volhard nie, omdat hulle hulself eerder as hul huweliksmaat liefhet.

d.) Dit faal nooit nie, omdat God die bron daarvan is.

Profesieë faal.

Tale faal.

Kennis verdwyn.

Ware Bybelse liefde gee nooit moed op nie. Dit faal nooit nie; daarom kan dit nooit oorwin word nie.

Liefde kan nie deur welsprekendheid verkry word nie. Dit kan nie deur wilskrag verower word nie. Dit kan nie deur onderrig aangeleer word nie, en dit kan nie deur menslike opoffering gekoop word nie. Dit is nie te koop nie, en dit kan ook nie soos ’n handelsware verruil word nie, want dit is geestelik van aard. Liefde kan slegs ontvang word van die Groot Ewige Gewer, deur dié wat waardig is om sulke krag en heerlikheid in hulle harte te besit.

Die opregtheid van my persoonlike strewe om die liefde van Christus met my hart na te jaag en te begryp, sal die hoeveelheid en gehalte van my liefde vir ander bepaal. Dit was Paulus se opregte uitroep aan die Filippense: “...dat ek Hom kan ken”.

Manne en vroue, toe julle mekaar die eerste keer ontmoet het, was julle liefde baie onvolwasse. Julle het dit gesien soos deur ’n spieël, dof, of soos ’n swak weerkaatsing in ’n spieël. Julle het oor die toekoms van julle liefde gepraat soos onvolwasse kinders wat geen ervaring daarvan gehad het nie. Julle het begin om daarvan te weet en daaroor te profeteer. Noudat julle getroud is, weet julle baie meer van LIEFDE as voorheen, maar daar is nog soveel meer om te leer. My vriende, mag die spieël vir julle helderder word namate julle volwasse word, en mag julle liefde in sy volmaaktheid in die dae wat kom, verstaan. Maar die pad van die regverdiges is soos die helder lig wat al helderder word tot die volle dag –Spreuke 4:18.

Manne en vroue, die beste ding wat julle vir mekaar kan doen, is om ’n daaglikse verhouding met die Here Jesus Christus na te streef. Onthou dat enige sukses in die lewe oefening verg. Oefen om mekaar lief te hê. Wees geduldig, vriendelik, vrygewig, nederig en onselfsugtig. Moedig mekaar in alle opregtheid aan om julle harte aan die heerskappy van Jesus Christus oor te gee, en julle huwelik sal alles wat julle ooit gedink het, oortref. ’n Jong man het eens gebid... “Here, stuur vir my ’n vrou wat U liefhet, want ek weet dat as sy U liefhet, sy my ook sal liefhê.” Hy was ’n wyse man.

Groot liefde kom teen ’n groot prys. Dit het die Here Jesus Christus sy lewe gekos. Eers nadat julle julle harte in volle vertroue aan die Here gegee het, sal julle julle harte aan mekaar kan gee. Julle het reeds alles verkry; daarom het julle niks om te verloor deur alles in ’n aardse verhouding te gee nie. Dit is die prys van liefde, en dit is die moeite werd. Liefde is lewe en lewe is liefde. Dit is beter om nie te lewe nie as om nie lief te hê nie. As daar liefde in julle huis is, sal julle ’n lewenskragtige doel hê om voor te lewe, en sal alles goed wees. Stel julle hoop en geloof in die God van Liefde, en julle sal... die Grootste Ding in die Wêreld vind.

Geliefdes, laat ons mekaar liefhê, want die liefde is uit God; en elkeen wat liefhet, is uit God gebore en ken God –1 Johannes 4:7.

Want alles wat uit God gebore is, oorwin die wêreld; en dit is die oorwinning wat die wêreld oorwin het, naamlik ons geloof –1 Johannes 5:4.

Mag God elke bruid en bruidegom seën.

    Have you ever tried to change the world? I have. As a teenager I dreamed of the daring exploits I was going to do for God. As I set the table in my parent’s house, I waited for the day when I would be able to do greater things—things like setting up house in Africa, speaking strange languages, and leading people to Jesus. The thought of living in a mud hut and dodging venomous snakes seemed thrilling.

    And then, part of my dreams came true! I left all I had ever known and had an adrenaline-fueled landing in an African country. I tried to change the small world I was in—that God-forsaken village full of drunkenness, broken marriages, fights, and neglected children. Daily I felt the angst of being so busy with “insignificant,” earthly tasks and wondered how to make a difference. Then suddenly, our labors were abruptly ended by burn-out and a host of government suspicions. None of this was in my dreams.

    I still ask the same question, “God, how can I make a difference?” The neighbor calls at the door. The laundry lady needs her pay. Lunch needs to be on the table in 15 minutes. Our fifth grader needs help with multiplying fractions. The sky fills up with dark clouds and the clothesline is full of laundry. I wipe the baby’s nose for the umpteenth time as she sits on top of the table disrupting her brother’s books and papers. I bake bread, make yogurt, and churn butter, and cook 21 meals a week. I fold mountains of laundry and the next week I do it all over again. I sweep the floor that has accumulated an astonishing amount of dirt in only two hours. In many ways, life is more mundane than it ever was before.

    I had no ability to change the world as a starry-eyed teen and neither do I have the ability now. God isn’t asking that of me. He only asks me to walk with Him and obey His voice. Slowly I am learning that the spiritual and physical are inseparable—even Jesus taught the gospel of the kingdom while resting, sleeping, and eating. Scrubbing a floor and slicing bread can be acts of worship to my Creator if I will deem them so. It is He who designed that my spiritual walk and the propagation thereof happens as my hands touch the earthly. This is how my spirit is refined. It’s the only way I can express my faith as a living faith. It’s the only way I can touch the hearts of my children and live out a practical gospel for them to imitate. It’s how my faith proves itself to be real to the unbeliever, as they see me struggle through the same things they do, along with my resulting responses.

    Slowly I am learning that serving God isn’t about determination or changing the world. It’s about allowing God’s spirit to inhabit me, guide me, and speak to me. I am learning that God is more interested in the person I am becoming instead of everything I want to do for Him. Perhaps I am after all just a smoking flax instead of the one who will change the world. I think Paul could relate to that feeling when he wrote, But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty; And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are: That no flesh should glory in his presence –1 Corinthians 1:27-29.

    Elisabeth Elliot said, “Sometimes the light rises excruciatingly slowly. The Kingdom of God is like leaven and seed, things which work silently, secretly, slowly, but there is in them an incalculable transforming power. Even in the plain soil, even in the dull dough, lies the possibility of transformation.”1

    To have my heart set on accomplishments and success is a selfish way to live. When that village and those people were taken from us in a whirl of government issues and misunderstandings, I felt like God couldn’t possibly use this for anyone’s good. He still needed us there, right? The fact is, He didn’t need us there anymore. We were not indispensable. Perhaps God allowed it all in order to learn that His acceptance of me is not based on my accomplishments.

    For who hath despised the day of small things… –Zechariah 4:10.

    Who am I to judge if a certain work is small or not? Am I restless with my duties, believing God would be more pleased with my perception of ‘great’ duties, seemingly always out of reach? Am I forgetting that serving Christ is not about me and my sense of fulfillment, it is about God and the work He wants to do through me?! Amy Carmichael said, “It is not the place where we are, or the work that we do or cannot do that matters, it is something else. It is the fire within that burns and shines, whatever be our circumstances.”2

    The fire that burns and shines within is our secret. That fire can burn while we scrub floors, cook endless meals, and home-school our children. It will touch the laundry lady, the house helper, the struggling girl at church and the neighbors. Sometimes it will happen sub-consciously, sometimes it happens if we decide to reach out instead of taking a nap or something else enjoyable, but always it takes forgetting ourselves, loving others, and noticing the small opportunities.

    But beware… we cannot confuse our resignation to the smallness in our lives, with lethargy. Too many Christians do not expect God to use them, so they settle into a lethargic spiritual position. We should expect God to work in amazing ways. God might use us to accomplish those things, but it often happens in ways we least think of or expect.

    The widow of Zarephath agreed to give her last handful of flour and the last remaining drops of oil to a stranger. She could have opposed the prophet and demanded he leave immediately, as after all, she was responsible for her son and that little bit of flour was all she had to give him. But no, she chose to give it all. God blessed her willing obedience by miraculously replenishing her flour and oil as long as she needed it.3

    God kept culling Gideon’s army until he eventually fought and won the battle with just a few hundred men. Normally, Gideon was accustomed to armies of thousands. and now God was asking him to fight a momentous battle with only a few hundred. In the end, this human impossibility became an opportunity for God to show his power.4

    At the beginning of His ministry, Jesus chose only twelve men to disciple, instead of the crowds. In the end, His small band of men deserted Him. He was mocked and killed. To everyone looking on, the remains of Jesus’ work seemed to have died with Him, yet the cosmic plan of redemption was being put into effect—those simple fishermen turned the world upside down with the gospel.5

    We see from these examples that God is not looking for the biggest, the strongest, or the best. He doesn’t only use people with specialized skills or impressive gifts. Our strength and resources are often like the few hundred soldiers in Gideon’s army—simply not enough for the need. But when we give what we have with a willing heart, God multiplies our small efforts into a showcase of His grace—a showcase meant for Him, often not visible to others. The simple act of setting a table is an act of faith, of giving, of service, no matter where we are. God has chosen these weak things to be significant in His kingdom.

    The secret to a successful life is Jesus in us, not our preconceived ideas of success. With Him working in and through us, His power will burn in our homes and neighborhoods. When He is the reason that we are living, we can trust Him with the outcome. Listening to the voice of Jesus, we can make a difference—one person, one encounter, one small thing at a time.

    2. Amy Carmichael, Edges of His Ways, pg 218
    3. 1 Kings 17: 11-16
    4. Judges 7
    5. Luke 6:13-16, John 19

    Hast du jemals versucht, die Welt zu verändern? Ich schon. Als Teenager träumte ich von den kühnen Taten, die ich für Gott vollbringen würde. Während ich bei meinen Eltern den Tisch deckte, wartete ich auf den Tag, an dem ich größere Dinge tun könnte – Dinge wie in Afrika einen Haushalt zu gründen, fremde Sprachen zu sprechen und Menschen zu Jesus zu führen. Der Gedanke, in einer Lehmhütte zu leben und Giftschlangen auszuweichen, erschien mir aufregend.

    Und dann ging ein Teil meiner Träume in Erfüllung! Ich ließ alles zurück, was ich je gekannt hatte, und landete voller Adrenalin in einem afrikanischen Land. Ich versuchte, die kleine Welt zu verändern, in der ich mich befand – jenes gottverlassene Dorf voller Trunksucht, zerrütteter Ehen, Streit und vernachlässigter Kinder. Tag für Tag spürte ich die Angst darüber, mit „unbedeutenden“, irdischen Aufgaben so beschäftigt zu sein, und fragte mich, wie ich etwas bewirken könnte. Dann wurden unsere Bemühungen ganz plötzlich durch ein Burn-out und eine Vielzahl von Verdächtigungen seitens der Regierung abrupt beendet. Nichts davon war Teil meiner Träume.

    Ich stelle immer noch dieselbe Frage: „Gott, wie kann ich etwas bewirken?“ Die Nachbarin klopft an die Tür. Die Frau, die für uns die Wäsche macht, muss bezahlt werden. In 15 Minuten muss das Mittagessen auf dem Tisch stehen. Unser Kind in der fünften Klasse braucht Hilfe beim Multiplizieren von Brüchen. Der Himmel füllt sich mit dunklen Wolken, und die Wäscheleine hängt voller Wäsche. Zum x-ten Mal wische ich dem Baby die Nase ab, während es auf dem Tisch sitzt und die Bücher und Papiere seines Bruders durcheinanderbringt. Ich backe Brot, mache Joghurt, schlage Butter und koche 21 Mahlzeiten pro Woche. Ich falte Berge von Wäsche, und in der nächsten Woche mache ich alles wieder von vorn. Ich fege den Boden, auf dem sich in nur zwei Stunden erstaunlich viel Schmutz angesammelt hat. In vielerlei Hinsicht ist das Leben alltäglicher als je zuvor.

    Als verträumte Teenagerin konnte ich die Welt nicht verändern, und heute kann ich es ebenso wenig. Gott verlangt das nicht von mir. Er bittet mich nur, mit ihm zu gehen und seiner Stimme zu gehorchen. Nach und nach lerne ich, dass das Geistliche und das Körperliche untrennbar miteinander verbunden sind – sogar Jesus verkündete das Evangelium vom Reich Gottes, während er ruhte, schlief und aß. Einen Boden zu schrubben und Brot zu schneiden kann ein Akt der Anbetung meines Schöpfers sein, wenn ich es so betrachte. Er hat es so eingerichtet, dass mein geistlicher Wandel und dessen Weitergabe geschehen, während meine Hände mit dem Irdischen beschäftigt sind. So wird mein Geist geformt. Nur so kann ich meinen Glauben als lebendigen Glauben zum Ausdruck bringen. Nur so kann ich die Herzen meiner Kinder berühren und ihnen ein praktisches Evangelium vorleben, dem sie nacheifern können. So erweist sich mein Glaube für den Ungläubigen als echt, wenn er sieht, wie ich dieselben Dinge durchlebe wie er und wie ich darauf reagiere.

    Nach und nach lerne ich, dass es beim Dienen für Gott nicht um Entschlossenheit oder darum geht, die Welt zu verändern. Es geht darum, Gottes Geist in mir wohnen, mich leiten und zu mir sprechen zu lassen. Ich lerne, dass Gott mehr daran interessiert ist, zu welchem Menschen ich werde, als an allem, was ich für ihn tun möchte. Vielleicht bin ich am Ende doch nur ein glimmender Docht und nicht diejenige, die die Welt verändern wird. Ich denke, Paulus hätte dieses Gefühl nachvollziehen können, als er schrieb: Gott hat das Törichte in der Welt erwählt, um die Weisen zuschanden zu machen; und Gott hat das Schwache in der Welt erwählt, um das Starke zuschanden zu machen; und das Niedrige in der Welt und das Verachtete hat Gott erwählt, ja, das, was nichts gilt, um das zunichtezumachen, was etwas gilt, damit sich kein Mensch vor ihm rühme – 1. Korinther 1,27-29.

    Elisabeth Elliot sagte: „Manchmal steigt das Licht quälend langsam auf. Das Reich Gottes ist wie Sauerteig und wie ein Samenkorn – Dinge, die lautlos, verborgen und langsam wirken, aber in sich eine unermessliche verwandelnde Kraft tragen. Selbst im schlichten Erdreich, selbst im faden Teig liegt die Möglichkeit der Verwandlung.“1

    Wenn mein Herz auf Erfolge und Errungenschaften ausgerichtet ist, lebe ich auf selbstsüchtige Weise. Als man uns jenes Dorf und jene Menschen in einem Wirbel aus Problemen mit der Regierung und Missverständnissen wegnahm, hatte ich das Gefühl, Gott könne das unmöglich zum Guten für irgendjemanden wenden. Er brauchte uns doch noch dort, oder? Tatsache ist: Er brauchte uns dort nicht mehr. Wir waren nicht unentbehrlich. Vielleicht ließ Gott all das zu, damit ich lernte, dass seine Annahme meiner Person nicht auf meinen Leistungen beruht.

    Wer hat den Tag geringer Dinge verachtet? … – Sacharja 4,10.

    Wer bin ich, zu beurteilen, ob eine bestimmte Arbeit gering ist oder nicht? Bin ich unzufrieden mit meinen Pflichten und glaube, Gott wäre mehr erfreut über meine Vorstellung von „großen“ Aufgaben, die scheinbar immer unerreichbar bleiben? Vergesse ich, dass es beim Dienen für Christus nicht um mich und mein Gefühl der Erfüllung geht, sondern um Gott und das Werk, das er durch mich tun möchte?! Amy Carmichael sagte: „Nicht der Ort, an dem wir sind, und nicht die Arbeit, die wir tun oder nicht tun können, ist entscheidend; es ist etwas anderes. Es ist das Feuer in uns, das brennt und leuchtet, was immer unsere Umstände sein mögen.“2

    Das Feuer, das in uns brennt und leuchtet, ist unser Geheimnis. Dieses Feuer kann brennen, während wir Böden schrubben, unzählige Mahlzeiten kochen und unsere Kinder zu Hause unterrichten. Es wird die Frau berühren, die für uns die Wäsche macht, die Haushaltshilfe, das Mädchen aus der Gemeinde, das zu kämpfen hat, und die Nachbarn. Manchmal geschieht das unbewusst; manchmal geschieht es, wenn wir uns entscheiden, auf andere zuzugehen, statt ein Nickerchen zu machen oder etwas anderes Angenehmes zu tun. Doch immer müssen wir dabei uns selbst vergessen, andere lieben und die kleinen Gelegenheiten wahrnehmen.

    Aber Vorsicht … wir dürfen unsere Ergebung in die Unscheinbarkeit unseres Lebens nicht mit Trägheit verwechseln. Zu viele Christen erwarten nicht, dass Gott sie gebraucht, und richten sich deshalb in einer geistlich trägen Haltung ein. Wir sollten erwarten, dass Gott auf erstaunliche Weise wirkt. Gott mag uns gebrauchen, um solche Dinge zu vollbringen, doch oft geschieht es auf eine Weise, an die wir am wenigsten denken oder die wir am wenigsten erwarten.

    Die Witwe von Sarepta erklärte sich bereit, einem Fremden ihre letzte Handvoll Mehl und die letzten verbliebenen Tropfen Öl zu geben. Sie hätte dem Propheten widersprechen und verlangen können, dass er sofort geht, denn schließlich war sie für ihren Sohn verantwortlich, und dieses bisschen Mehl war alles, was sie ihm zu geben hatte. Aber nein, sie entschied sich, alles herzugeben. Gott segnete ihren bereitwilligen Gehorsam, indem er ihr Mehl und Öl auf wunderbare Weise immer wieder auffüllte, solange sie es brauchte.3

    Gott ließ Gideons Heer immer weiter schrumpfen, bis Gideon schließlich mit nur wenigen Hundert Männern kämpfte und die Schlacht gewann. Normalerweise war Gideon an Heere von Tausenden gewöhnt. Und nun bat Gott ihn, eine gewaltige Schlacht mit nur wenigen Hundert zu führen. Am Ende wurde diese menschlich gesehen unmögliche Aufgabe zu einer Gelegenheit für Gott, seine Macht zu zeigen.4

    Zu Beginn seines Wirkens wählte Jesus nur zwölf Männer aus, die er zu Jüngern machen wollte, statt sich an die Menschenmengen zu wenden. Am Ende verließen ihn seine kleine Schar von Männern. Er wurde verspottet und getötet. Für alle, die zusahen, schien der Rest von Jesu Werk mit ihm gestorben zu sein; doch der kosmische Erlösungsplan wurde gerade in die Tat umgesetzt – diese einfachen Fischer stellten mit dem Evangelium die Welt auf den Kopf.5

    An diesen Beispielen sehen wir, dass Gott nicht nach den Größten, Stärksten oder Besten Ausschau hält. Er gebraucht nicht nur Menschen mit besonderen Fähigkeiten oder beeindruckenden Gaben. Unsere Kraft und unsere Mittel reichen oft ebenso wenig aus wie die wenigen Hundert Soldaten in Gideons Heer. Doch wenn wir mit willigem Herzen geben, was wir haben, macht Gott aus unseren kleinen Bemühungen ein Schaufenster seiner Gnade – ein Schaufenster, das für ihn bestimmt und für andere oft nicht sichtbar ist. Einen Tisch zu decken ist ein einfacher Akt des Glaubens, des Gebens und des Dienens, ganz gleich, wo wir sind. Gott hat diese schwachen Dinge erwählt, damit sie in seinem Reich Bedeutung haben.

    Das Geheimnis eines erfüllten Lebens ist Jesus in uns, nicht unsere vorgefassten Vorstellungen von Erfolg. Wenn er in uns und durch uns wirkt, wird seine Kraft in unseren Häusern und Nachbarschaften brennen. Wenn er der Grund ist, warum wir leben, können wir ihm das Ergebnis anvertrauen. Wenn wir auf die Stimme Jesu hören, können wir etwas bewirken – einen Menschen, eine Begegnung, eine kleine Sache nach der anderen.

    1. Elisabeth Elliot, The Savage My Kinsman (überarbeitete Ausgabe, Servant Publications, 1981), Nachwort, S. 147
    2. Amy Carmichael, Edges of His Ways, S. 218
    3. 1. Könige 17: 11-16
    4. Richter 7
    5. Lukas 6:13-16, Johannes 19

    Har du någonsin försökt förändra världen? Det har jag. Som tonåring drömde jag om de djärva bedrifter jag skulle utföra för Gud. När jag dukade bordet hemma hos mina föräldrar väntade jag på dagen då jag skulle kunna göra större saker – sådant som att slå mig ner i Afrika, tala främmande språk och leda människor till Jesus. Tanken på att bo i en lerhydda och väja för giftormar verkade spännande.

    Och sedan blev en del av mina drömmar verklighet! Jag lämnade allt jag någonsin känt till och landade i ett afrikanskt land med adrenalinet pumpande. Jag försökte förändra den lilla värld jag befann mig i – den gudsförgätna byn full av fylleri, trasiga äktenskap, bråk och försummade barn. Varje dag kände jag våndan över att vara så upptagen med ”obetydliga”, jordiska sysslor och undrade hur jag skulle kunna göra skillnad. Sedan tog vårt arbete plötsligt abrupt slut på grund av utbrändhet och en mängd misstankar från myndigheterna. Inget av detta fanns med i mina drömmar.

    Jag ställer fortfarande samma fråga: ”Gud, hur kan jag göra skillnad?” Grannen knackar på dörren. Tvättkvinnan behöver få sin lön. Lunchen måste stå på bordet om 15 minuter. Vår femteklassare behöver hjälp med att multiplicera bråk. Himlen fylls av mörka moln och tvättlinan är full av tvätt. Jag torkar babyn om näsan för femtioelfte gången medan hon sitter uppe på bordet och stökar till sin brors böcker och papper. Jag bakar bröd, gör yoghurt, kärnar smör och lagar 21 måltider i veckan. Jag viker berg av tvätt, och veckan därpå gör jag om alltihop. Jag sopar golvet, som på bara två timmar har samlat en häpnadsväckande mängd smuts. På många sätt är livet mer vardagligt än det någonsin varit förut.

    Jag hade ingen förmåga att förändra världen som en drömsk tonåring, och det har jag inte nu heller. Gud ber mig inte om det. Han ber mig bara att vandra med honom och lyda hans röst. Sakta lär jag mig att det andliga och det fysiska är oskiljaktiga – till och med Jesus förkunnade evangeliet om riket medan han vilade, sov och åt. Att skura ett golv och skära upp bröd kan vara tillbedjan av min Skapare, om jag väljer att se det så. Det är han som har utformat det så att min andliga vandring och dess spridning sker när mina händer rör vid det jordiska. Så förädlas min ande. Det är det enda sättet jag kan uttrycka min tro som en levande tro. Det är det enda sättet jag kan beröra mina barns hjärtan och leva ut ett praktiskt evangelium som de kan ta efter. Så visar sig min tro vara verklig för den som inte tror, när de ser mig kämpa med samma saker som de gör, och ser hur jag reagerar på dem.

    Sakta lär jag mig att tjänandet av Gud inte handlar om beslutsamhet eller om att förändra världen. Det handlar om att låta Guds ande bo i mig, vägleda mig och tala till mig. Jag lär mig att Gud är mer intresserad av den person jag håller på att bli än av allt jag vill göra för honom. Kanske är jag trots allt bara en rykande veke och inte den som ska förändra världen. Jag tror att Paulus kunde känna igen sig i den känslan när han skrev: Men det som är dåraktigt i världen har Gud utvalt för att göra de visa till skam, och det som är svagt i världen har Gud utvalt för att göra det starka till skam. Det som är obetydligt i världen och det som föraktas, ja, det som inte finns till, har Gud utvalt för att göra det som finns till intet, så att ingen människa ska berömma sig inför honom – 1 Korinthierbrevet 1:27-29.

    Elisabeth Elliot sade: ”Ibland stiger ljuset fram plågsamt långsamt. Guds rike är som surdeg och frö, sådant som verkar tyst, i det fördolda och långsamt, men som bär på en omätbar förvandlande kraft. Även i den enkla jorden, även i den sega degen, ligger möjligheten till förvandling.”1

    Att låta mitt hjärta vara fäst vid prestationer och framgång är ett själviskt sätt att leva. När den byn och människorna där rycktes ifrån oss i en virvel av myndighetsproblem och missförstånd kändes det som om Gud omöjligen kunde använda detta till någons bästa. Han behövde väl oss där fortfarande? Faktum är att han inte längre behövde oss där. Vi var inte oumbärliga. Kanske tillät Gud allt detta för att jag skulle lära mig att hans godkännande av mig inte grundar sig på mina prestationer.

    Vem har föraktat den ringa begynnelsens dag … – Sakarja 4:10.

Glömmer jag att tjänandet av Kristus inte handlar om mig och min känsla av tillfredsställelse, utan om Gud och det verk han vill utföra genom mig?! Amy Carmichael sade: ”Det är inte platsen där vi befinner oss eller arbetet vi utför eller inte kan utföra som betyder något, utan något annat. Det är elden inom oss som brinner och lyser, oavsett våra omständigheter.”2

Den kommer att beröra tvättkvinnan, hushållshjälpen, flickan i församlingen som kämpar och grannarna. Ibland sker det omedvetet, ibland sker det om vi bestämmer oss för att sträcka ut en hand i stället för att ta en tupplur eller göra något annat trevligt, men alltid kräver det att vi glömmer oss själva, älskar andra och lägger märke till de små tillfällena.

Vår styrka och våra resurser är ofta som de få hundra soldaterna i Gideons här – helt enkelt otillräckliga för behovet. Men när vi ger det vi har med villigt hjärta mångfaldigar Gud våra små ansträngningar till en uppvisning av hans nåd – en uppvisning avsedd för honom, ofta osynlig för andra. Att helt enkelt duka ett bord är en trosgärning, en gåva och en tjänst, oavsett var vi befinner oss. Gud har valt dessa svaga ting till att vara betydelsefulla i hans rike.

    Hemligheten bakom ett framgångsrikt liv är Jesus i oss, inte våra förutfattade meningar om framgång. När han verkar i och genom oss kommer hans kraft att brinna i våra hem och kvarter. När han är orsaken till att vi lever kan vi lita på honom när det gäller resultatet. När vi lyssnar till Jesu röst kan vi göra skillnad – en människa, ett möte, en liten sak i taget.

    3. 1 Kungaboken 17: 11-16
    4. Domarboken 7
    5. Lukas 6:13-16, Johannes 19

Have you ever tried to change the world? I have. As a teenager I dreamed of the daring exploits I was going to do for God. As I set the table in my parent’s house, I waited for the day when I would be able to do greater things—things like setting up house in Africa, speaking strange languages, and leading people to Jesus. The thought of living in a mud hut and dodging venomous snakes seemed thrilling.

And then, part of my dreams came true! I left all I had ever known and had an adrenaline-fueled landing in an African country. I tried to change the small world I was in—that God-forsaken village full of drunkenness, broken marriages, fights, and neglected children. Daily I felt the angst of being so busy with “insignificant,” earthly tasks and wondered how to make a difference. Then suddenly, our labors were abruptly ended by burn-out and a host of government suspicions. None of this was in my dreams.

I still ask the same question, “God, how can I make a difference?” The neighbor calls at the door. The laundry lady needs her pay. Lunch needs to be on the table in 15 minutes. Our fifth grader needs help with multiplying fractions. The sky fills up with dark clouds and the clothesline is full of laundry. I wipe the baby’s nose for the umpteenth time as she sits on top of the table disrupting her brother’s books and papers. I bake bread, make yogurt, and churn butter, and cook 21 meals a week. I fold mountains of laundry and the next week I do it all over again. I sweep the floor that has accumulated an astonishing amount of dirt in only two hours. In many ways, life is more mundane than it ever was before.

I had no ability to change the world as a starry-eyed teen and neither do I have the ability now. God isn’t asking that of me. He only asks me to walk with Him and obey His voice. Slowly I am learning that the spiritual and physical are inseparable—even Jesus taught the gospel of the kingdom while resting, sleeping, and eating. Scrubbing a floor and slicing bread can be acts of worship to my Creator if I will deem them so. It is He who designed that my spiritual walk and the propagation thereof happens as my hands touch the earthly. This is how my spirit is refined. It’s the only way I can express my faith as a living faith. It’s the only way I can touch the hearts of my children and live out a practical gospel for them to imitate. It’s how my faith proves itself to be real to the unbeliever, as they see me struggle through the same things they do, along with my resulting responses.

Slowly I am learning that serving God isn’t about determination or changing the world. It’s about allowing God’s spirit to inhabit me, guide me, and speak to me. I am learning that God is more interested in the person I am becoming instead of everything I want to do for Him. Perhaps I am after all just a smoking flax instead of the one who will change the world. I think Paul could relate to that feeling when he wrote, But God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to confound the wise; and God hath chosen the weak things of the world to confound the things which are mighty; And base things of the world, and things which are despised, hath God chosen, yea, and things which are not, to bring to nought things that are: That no flesh should glory in his presence –1 Corinthians 1:27-29.

Elisabeth Elliot said, “Sometimes the light rises excruciatingly slowly. The Kingdom of God is like leaven and seed, things which work silently, secretly, slowly, but there is in them an incalculable transforming power. Even in the plain soil, even in the dull dough, lies the possibility of transformation.”1

To have my heart set on accomplishments and success is a selfish way to live. When that village and those people were taken from us in a whirl of government issues and misunderstandings, I felt like God couldn’t possibly use this for anyone’s good. He still needed us there, right? The fact is, He didn’t need us there anymore. We were not indispensable. Perhaps God allowed it all in order to learn that His acceptance of me is not based on my accomplishments.

For who hath despised the day of small things… –Zechariah 4:10.

Who am I to judge if a certain work is small or not? Am I restless with my duties, believing God would be more pleased with my perception of ‘great’ duties, seemingly always out of reach? Am I forgetting that serving Christ is not about me and my sense of fulfillment, it is about God and the work He wants to do through me?! Amy Carmichael said, “It is not the place where we are, or the work that we do or cannot do that matters, it is something else. It is the fire within that burns and shines, whatever be our circumstances.”2

The fire that burns and shines within is our secret. That fire can burn while we scrub floors, cook endless meals, and home-school our children. It will touch the laundry lady, the house helper, the struggling girl at church and the neighbors. Sometimes it will happen sub-consciously, sometimes it happens if we decide to reach out instead of taking a nap or something else enjoyable, but always it takes forgetting ourselves, loving others, and noticing the small opportunities.

But beware… we cannot confuse our resignation to the smallness in our lives, with lethargy. Too many Christians do not expect God to use them, so they settle into a lethargic spiritual position. We should expect God to work in amazing ways. God might use us to accomplish those things, but it often happens in ways we least think of or expect.

The widow of Zarephath agreed to give her last handful of flour and the last remaining drops of oil to a stranger. 저는 여전히 같은 질문을 합니다. “하나님, 제가 어떻게 변화를 가져올 수 있을까요?” 이웃이 문을 두드립니다. 세탁 일을 하는 분에게 품삯을 드려야 합니다. 15분 뒤면 점심을 식탁에 올려야 합니다. 초등학교 5학년인 아이는 분수의 곱셈을 도와 달라고 합니다. 하늘에는 먹구름이 가득하고 빨랫줄에는 빨래가 가득 걸려 있습니다. 아기는 식탁 위에 앉아 오빠의 책과 종이를 어지럽히고, 저는 수없이 반복해 아기의 코를 닦아 줍니다. 빵을 굽고, 요구르트를 만들고, 버터를 휘저어 만들고, 일주일에 21끼를 요리합니다. 산처럼 쌓인 빨래를 개고 나면, 다음 주에 다시 처음부터 똑같은 일을 합니다. 겨우 두 시간 만에 놀랄 만큼 먼지가 쌓인 바닥을 쓸어 냅니다. 여러모로 지금의 삶은 예전보다 훨씬 더 단조롭습니다.

반짝이는 눈을 가진 십 대였을 때도 세상을 바꿀 능력은 없었고, 지금도 제게는 그런 능력이 없습니다. 하나님은 제게 그런 일을 요구하지 않으십니다. 하나님은 그저 제가 그분과 동행하고 그분의 음성에 순종하기를 바라십니다. 저는 영적인 것과 육적인 것이 서로 떼어 놓을 수 없다는 사실을 서서히 배우고 있습니다. 예수님께서도 쉬고, 잠자고, 식사하시면서 하나님 나라의 복음을 가르치셨습니다. 제가 그렇게 여기기만 한다면, 바닥을 문지르고 빵을 써는 일도 창조주께 드리는 예배가 될 수 있습니다. 제가 세상적인 일을 하며 손을 움직일 때 영적 여정과 그 여정의 확장이 이루어지도록 설계하신 분은 바로 하나님이십니다. 이것이 제 영이 다듬어지는 방식입니다. 제 믿음을 살아 있는 믿음으로 드러낼 수 있는 유일한 길입니다. 제 자녀들의 마음에 닿고, 아이들이 본받을 수 있는 실제적인 복음을 살아 내는 유일한 길입니다. 믿지 않는 사람들이 제가 그들과 같은 일들을 겪으며 고군분투하고, 그에 따라 어떻게 반응하는지를 볼 때, 제 믿음이 참된 것임을 보여 주는 길입니다.

하나님을 섬기는 일은 결심을 굳게 하거나 세상을 바꾸는 일이 아니라는 것을 저는 서서히 배우고 있습니다. 하나님의 영이 제 안에 거하시며, 저를 인도하고 제게 말씀하시도록 하는 일입니다. 하나님께서는 제가 그분을 위해 하고 싶은 모든 일보다, 제가 어떤 사람으로 자라 가는지에 더 관심이 있으시다는 것을 배우고 있습니다. 어쩌면 저는 결국 세상을 바꿀 사람이 아니라, 연기 나는 심지에 불과할지도 모릅니다. 바울도 이런 마음을 알았으리라 생각합니다. 그가 이렇게 썼기 때문입니다. 그러나 하나님께서는 지혜로운 자들을 부끄럽게 하시려고 세상의 어리석은 것들을 택하셨으며, 강한 것들을 부끄럽게 하시려고 세상의 약한 것들을 택하셨습니다. 또한 하나님께서는 있는 것들을 무력하게 하시려고 세상의 천한 것들과 멸시받는 것들, 곧 없는 것들을 택하셨습니다. 이는 아무 육체도 그분 앞에서 자랑하지 못하게 하려는 것입니다. –고린도전서 1:27-29.

엘리자베스 엘리엇은 이렇게 말했습니다. “때로 빛은 고통스러울 만큼 천천히 떠오릅니다. 하나님 나라는 누룩과 씨앗과 같습니다. 그것들은 조용히, 은밀히, 천천히 작용하지만, 헤아릴 수 없이 큰 변화의 힘을 품고 있습니다. 평범한 흙에도, 질척한 반죽에도 변화의 가능성이 놓여 있습니다.”1

성취와 성공에 마음을 두는 것은 이기적인 삶의 방식입니다. 정부의 여러 문제와 오해가 뒤엉켜 그 마을과 사람들을 우리에게서 앗아 갔을 때, 저는 하나님께서 이 일을 누구에게든 유익하게 사용하실 리 없다고 느꼈습니다. 하나님께서는 여전히 우리가 그곳에 있기를 바라셨던 것 아닌가요? 사실 하나님께서는 더 이상 그곳에서 우리를 필요로 하지 않으셨습니다. 우리는 없어서는 안 될 사람들이 아니었습니다. 어쩌면 하나님께서는 그 모든 일을 허락하심으로써, 하나님께서 저를 받아 주시는 것이 제 성취에 달려 있지 않다는 사실을 배우게 하셨는지도 모릅니다.

작은 일의 날을 멸시하는 자가 누구냐… –스가랴 4:10.

어떤 일이 작은지 아닌지를 제가 판단할 수 있겠습니까? 하나님께서 ‘위대한’ 일이라고 생각하는 의무라면 더 기뻐하실 거라고 여기며, 늘 손에 닿지 않는 듯한 그 일을 바라느라 제가 맡은 일에 안달하고 있지는 않습니까? 그리스도를 섬기는 것은 저와 제 성취감에 관한 일이 아니라 하나님과 그분께서 저를 통해 하시려는 일에 관한 것임을 잊고 있지는 않습니까?! 에이미 카마이클은 이렇게 말했습니다. “우리가 있는 장소나 우리가 하는 일, 혹은 할 수 없는 일이 중요한 것이 아닙니다. 중요한 것은 다른 것입니다. 우리 안에서 타오르며 빛나는 불, 그것이 우리의 상황이 어떠하든 중요합니다.”2

우리 안에서 타오르며 빛나는 불이 우리의 비밀입니다. 그 불은 우리가 바닥을 문지르고, 끝없이 식사를 준비하고, 집에서 아이들을 가르치는 동안에도 타오를 수 있습니다. 그 불은 세탁 일을 하는 분과 집안일을 도와주는 분, 교회에서 어려움을 겪는 자매와 이웃들의 마음에 닿을 것입니다. 때로는 자신도 모르는 사이에 그런 일이 일어나고, 때로는 낮잠이나 그 밖의 즐거운 일을 택하는 대신 손을 내밀기로 할 때 그런 일이 일어납니다. 하지만 언제나 자신을 잊고, 다른 사람들을 사랑하며, 작은 기회들을 알아차려야 합니다.

하지만 조심하십시오… 우리 삶의 작은 것들에 체념하는 태도를 무기력과 혼동해서는 안 됩니다. 너무나 많은 그리스도인이 하나님께서 자신들을 사용하실 것이라고 기대하지 않고, 영적으로 무기력한 상태에 안주합니다. 우리는 하나님께서 놀라운 방식으로 일하시리라고 기대해야 합니다. 하나님께서 우리를 사용해 그런 일들을 이루실 수도 있지만, 그런 일은 우리가 가장 생각지 못하거나 예상하지 못한 방식으로 일어나는 경우가 많습니다.

사르밧의 과부는 낯선 사람에게 마지막 한 줌의 밀가루와 남아 있던 기름 몇 방울을 주기로 했습니다. 그 여인은 선지자에게 맞서 당장 떠나라고 요구할 수도 있었습니다. 어쨌든 아들을 책임져야 했고, 그 조금 남은 밀가루는 아들에게 줄 수 있는 전부였기 때문입니다. 그러나 그러지 않았습니다. 그 여인은 모두 내어 주기로 했습니다. 하나님께서는 그 여인의 기꺼운 순종을 기뻐 받으시고, 필요한 동안 밀가루와 기름이 기적적으로 떨어지지 않게 하셔서 복을 주셨습니다.3

하나님께서는 기드온의 군대를 계속 줄이셔서, 마침내 그는 겨우 수백 명의 병사만으로 전쟁을 치러 승리했습니다. 기드온은 보통 수천 명의 군대를 상대하는 데 익숙했습니다. 그런데 이제 하나님께서는 그에게 겨우 수백 명만으로 중대한 전투를 치르라고 하셨습니다. 결국 인간의 힘으로는 불가능해 보이는 이 일이 하나님께서 자신의 능력을 보여 주실 기회가 되었습니다.4

사역을 시작하실 때 예수님께서는 무리를 제자로 삼는 대신 열두 사람만 택하셨습니다. 결국 그 적은 수의 제자들은 예수님을 버렸습니다. 예수님은 조롱당하고 죽임을 당하셨습니다. 지켜보던 모든 사람에게 예수님의 사역은 그분과 함께 끝난 듯 보였지만, 우주적인 구속의 계획이 실행되고 있었습니다. 그 평범한 어부들이 복음으로 세상을 뒤집어 놓았습니다.5

이 사례들을 통해 하나님께서는 가장 크거나, 가장 강하거나, 가장 뛰어난 사람을 찾으시는 것이 아님을 알 수 있습니다. 하나님께서는 전문 기술이나 인상적인 은사를 가진 사람들만 사용하시는 것이 아닙니다. 우리의 힘과 자원은 흔히 기드온의 군대에 있던 수백 명의 병사처럼, 필요한 일을 감당하기에 턱없이 부족합니다. 그러나 우리가 기꺼운 마음으로 가진 것을 드릴 때, 하나님께서는 우리의 작은 노력을 자신의 은혜를 드러내는 본보기로 키워 주십니다. 그것은 하나님을 위한 본보기이며, 흔히 다른 사람들에게는 보이지 않습니다. 어디에 있든 식탁을 차리는 단순한 행위도 믿음과 나눔과 섬김의 행위입니다. 하나님께서는 이 약한 것들을 그분의 나라에서 중요한 것이 되도록 택하셨습니다.

성공적인 삶의 비결은 우리가 미리 정해 둔 성공의 관념이 아니라 우리 안에 계신 예수님입니다. 예수님께서 우리 안에서, 또 우리를 통해 일하시면 그분의 능력이 우리의 가정과 이웃 가운데 타오를 것입니다. 예수님이 우리가 살아가는 이유라면, 우리는 그 결과를 그분께 맡길 수 있습니다. 예수님의 음성에 귀 기울이며, 한 사람씩, 한 번의 만남씩, 한 가지 작은 일씩 변화를 가져올 수 있습니다.

  2. 에이미 카마이클, 『Edges of His Ways』, 218쪽
  3. 열왕기상 17: 11-16
  4. 사사기 7
  5. 누가복음 6:13-16, 요한복음 19
